correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the Poisson count gives uniform order statistics and hence a Dirichlet(1,...,1) gap vector. Inclusion-exclusion yields the exact largest-spacing mean H_m/m. Poissonization gives the exact mean t Ein(mu)/mu, and the standard Poisson score identity Cov(N,g(N))=mu dE[g(N)]/dmu then gives the covariance. Its strict negativity follows from the positive derivative of Ein(mu)-(1-exp(-mu)). All boundary cases, normalization, and small/large-mu asymptotics are handled explicitly.

value.rationale: Arrival count and longest idle interval are canonical complementary load/reliability observables of a Poisson process. The theorem converts the intuitive anticorrelation into an exact all-intensity law, exposes the decreasing conditional regression, and gives both sparse- and dense-arrival asymptotics. The dense-regime covariance grows logarithmically on the interarrival-time scale even though the longest gap itself shrinks, which is a nontrivial quantitative feature of the count-extreme coupling.
